thread:
alex: heads up — staging shows a new p99 regression under cont-batching when merges exceed ~8 reqs. tail spikes from 45ms -> 220ms. suspect KV cache fragmentation + a head-of-line blocking pattern during merge/backpressure.
maya: can you drop the flamegraph/profile link?
alex: here — running perf harness against canary: https://perf.redwood/staging/rl/4210009876
alex: flamegraph snippet (sampling):
```
merge_batch_loop  48%
  -> kv_slot_acquire 22%
  -> kv_reclaim_async 10%
  -> kv_fragment_coalesce 8%
  -> serialize_out 5%
```
alex: also seeing frequent "headskip" log lines around merges: `contbatch: headskip triggered for slot=0x7f9a` — looks like merge path is skipping some KV reuse which increases allocations.
simon: hmm. ive seen similar when async reclaim races with merge: if reclaim delays, fragments can't coalesce and later merges create small incompatible fragments, causing paging/evict churn.
kevin: can we try toggling merge_backoff_ms and the headskip fast-path? i'd run two builds: (A) merge_backoff_ms=3 -> reduce immediate merges; (B) disable headskip to force strict ordering. compare p95/p99 and allocated bytes.
alex: good plan. reproducer command I'm using: `./bin/perf_harness --qps 120 --seq-dist long --batch-mode continuous --merge-threshold 8 --duration 30m`
And to capture heap/kv stats: 
```bash
curl -s http://staging-metrics/kv | jq . > kv_metrics_before.json
./bin/perf_harness ...
curl -s http://staging-metrics/kv | jq . > kv_metrics_after.json
```
lisa: are we sure this is fragmentation and not just slower kernel selection under heavier merged batches? kernel choices can flip when sequence length distribution changes.
alex: good call — i profiled CPU: kernel selection is flat (we still pick the optimized fused-attn path). the alloc rate and slot churn increased though. from heap profiles: `kv_fragment_count` 12k -> 47k over 30m; resident set increased ~1.2GB for longctx tests.
ci-bot: deploy: canary runtime build 4210010000 queued (labels: contbatch-experiments). :gear:
simon: action item: add a counter for "kv_slot_reuse_miss" and a histogram for fragment sizes. also emit a trace span around merge->reclaim to see latencies.
maya: i'll run the two builds overnight and upload traces. also will validate with synthetic seed that forces reclamation frequency.
alex: if build (A) reduces p99 but increases tail allocations we might tune backoff dynamically. if (B) helps, perhaps headskip logic needs to check fragment compatibility not just slot availability.
kevin: also PR a tiny metric: `kv.merge.backpressure_duration_ms` — helps correlate when merges stall waiting on reclaim.
simon: i'll draft the instrumentation patch and link it here by EOD. expecting minimal perf hit for counters.
lisa: ping me when traces are up, i'll run kernel-level perf to rule out codegen regressions.
alex: thanks — assigning: simon (instrumentation), maya (canary runs + traces), kevin (experiment builds/ops), lisa (kernel perf check). will reconvene tomorrow 10:30am PT. :thumbsup:
